summary.intent: Audit whether the project's changesets (release notes) are well written and well positioned in the changelog, and ensure recent user-visible changes have proper changesets.
summary.outcome: Found the released changesets (0.2.0, 0.3.0) follow convention but #46 shipped without one; opened PR #48 with three changesets plus a CONTRIBUTING section, and sent changeset wording/format rules to the agents working on #45 and #43. Three agents are still running.

repo: Changesets follow the trail-152 convention: a lead sentence plus bold-led sub-bullets, one level of sub-bullets, no headings or leading '- ', identifiers in backticks.
Changelog entries render in filename order, not importance or bump-level order; a '0-' prefix makes an entry lead, and '1-' places it after, e.g. leading the patches.
The Changesets CI job does not require a changeset on PRs, so #46 (diagnostics, hints, exit codes) merged without one.
`callisto version --dry-run` prints only the version plan; rendered changelog text can only be seen by running `callisto version` in a scratch copy or in the release PR.
`callisto status --check --strict` validates changesets and shows the planned next version (0.3.0 -> 0.4.0 after PR #48).
One topic per changeset file is the repo convention.
workflow: Render the changelog in a scratch copy with `callisto version` to verify real ordering and formatting rather than guessing.
When parallel agents work on other open PRs, send them the changeset wording and format rules so each adds its own on its own branch.
Changelogs should state regressions plainly, e.g. that files over about 254 KiB are no longer parsed in #43.

friction: No preview of rendered changelog text without running the version command on a scratch copy, since --dry-run shows only the version plan.
Changeset ordering can only be controlled via filename prefixes, which is a hack.
CI did not enforce changesets, so #46 slipped through with no changelog entry.
open_items: Three agents are still running: #43 conflicts, #45 conflicts, and the docs/CI truth PR; results to be reported when they land.
#45 (four entries) and #43 (two entries) still need their changesets added on their own branches.
Suggested upstream Callisto change: sort entries by bump level then name so the filename hack is unnecessary (not touched, since it is the user's repo).
Optional lightweight CI check that PRs touching user-visible code include a changeset.
